whatItIs.text: A cold-water fish with mild flavour and dense, flaky white flesh — the classic of fish and chips, and the source of cod liver oil.

historyNote.text: Atlantic cod (named by Linnaeus in 1758) has fed Europe and North America for centuries, so heavily that the species is now listed as Vulnerable; Pacific cod carries much of the trade today.

howToChoose.text: Choose fillets that look wet and pearly, with firm flesh and a clean sea smell; thicker cuts from the head end hold together better in stews.

storage.text: Keep fish sealed on the bottom shelf, away from ready-to-eat food, or freeze on the day of purchase.

useItUp.text: Flake cod into fishcakes with mash and herbs, or stretch it into a chowder.

substitutions.note: sweeter, more delicate; the other chip-shop classic
same family, cheaper and slightly softer
